subject: Clarify customer keystore escrow, operator breakglass, and subprocessor geofence for on-prem deploy
messages:
From: security@medvox.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medvox.com, alex.smythe@medvox.com
Date: 2028-10-11T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on keystore escrow / operator access for on-prem private deployment

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — MedVox is enthusiastic about using Redwood Private in our clinic network. Before we move to procurement and legal sign-off, InfoSec has asked for a few clarifications on the sections of the draft DPA that cover key control, operator access, and subprocessors. High-level asks are below; I attached our preferred deployment diagram (onprem-data-flow_v2.pdf) for reference.

1) Customer keystore model: We need confirmation that customer-managed KEKs (customer-supplied KMS keys) can be used for all data-at-rest volumes and model artifacts, and that Redwood does not retain plaintext keys. If Redwood requires escrow for disaster recovery, please describe the escrow mechanism, who holds the escrow, and conditions for key release.

2) Operator/breakglass access: Under what scenarios can Redwood staff access decrypted data or the running host memory? We need strict, auditable breakglass definitions and an ops workflow with 2-way approvals (customer + Redwood) and immutable logs.

3) Subprocessors & geofence: Provide the current subprocessor list for Private deployments, including cloud partners used for optional telemetry and monitoring, and confirm whether any subprocessors may be located outside the US for backups/replication.

4) Auditability & logs: Level of audit logs available to the customer (KMS key usage, operator sessions, console/API activity), retention window, and whether logs can be exported to a customer-managed SIEM.

We want to avoid long legal redlines if we can agree on technical constraints first. Can someone on your team provide a short, actionable response and the latest subprocessor CSV? Also please indicate if you can accept a MedVox clause that operator access requires an explicit DocuSign approval per incident.

Best,
Alex Smythe
Head of Security, MedVox
security@medvox.com

Subject: Re: Questions on keystore escrow / operator access for on-prem private deployment

Thanks — technical detail below. I kept the response customer-facing but included notes on triggers and controls.

1) KEKs & escrow:
- Customer KEK: we support integration with customer-managed KMS (CloudKMS/HSM) via a vault-plugin so that KEKs never transit Redwood control plane in plaintext. Keys are used by the local host to unwrap data-encryption-keys (DEKs) at runtime.
- Escrow (optional): our escrow option encrypts a recovery envelope with a dual-control scheme: partial shares held by Redwood and a third-party escrow agent (TrustAudit). Release requires a signed approval from a designated customer admin plus Redwood incident lead, and an audit ticket. The escrow artifact is itself encrypted under the customer KEK so Redwood cannot unilaterally decrypt.

2) Operator/breakglass access:
- Normal ops: Redwood engineers have no access to plaintext DEKs or to replay-ready model input/output streams in normal operations.
- Breakglass: allowed only in a documented incident (catastrophic hardware failure or emergency data recovery) and requires:
  a) Customer request via an approved channel (DocuSign or signed ticket from customer admin)
  b) Redwood escalation runbook with at least two Redwood approvers present (infra lead + security)
  c) Live recorded session (screen + keystroke audit) with session transcript retained for 7 years
  d) All actions logged and exported to customer SIEM on request
- Technical controls: ephemeral, host-bound KMS unwrapping; no persistent plaintext caches; hardware memory scrubbing on process exit; encrypted swap.

3) Subprocessors & geofence:
- Current subprocessors CSV is attached. For standard Private deployments the only routinely involved subprocessors are: TrustAudit (escrow & attestation), LogFlux (optional hosted telemetry pipeline, only if customer opts in), and a partner cloud region for optional object-storage replication (only if configured).
- We can contractually geofence backups to US-only regions for MedVox; by default replication partners are region-aligned but we will accept a US-only geofence clause for this account.

4) Auditability & logs:
- We emit KMS usage events, operator session start/stop, API key creation events, and host-level system logs. Default retention is 90 days; archive to customer-managed S3 or SIEM is available via signed export for up to 7 years.

Notes: the most common negotiation points are (a) whether Redwood will accept customer-exclusive escrow (we can), and (b) whether operator access must be DocuSign-only. The DocuSign-only requirement creates operational friction but we can accept DocuSign as an authorized approval method if the contract enumerates acceptable signer roles and SLA windows for emergency access.

Attaching: subprocessors_export_20281010.csv (redacted), sample-operator-session-log-schema.csv, onprem-data-flow_v2.pdf.

—Karthik
Principal Infra/Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on keystore escrow / operator access for on-prem private deployment

Stephanie / KarThik — drafting a concise amendment to the DPA that captures MedVox's requirements without creating an unworkable operations burden. Two proposed bullets below (we can iterate):

1) Operator Access: Redwood will not access customer plaintext data or decrypted model artifacts except under documented emergency circumstances ("Breakglass Events"). Breakglass Events require both (i) a signed direction from a named customer admin provided in advance and (ii) an internal Redwood dual-approver authorization. All access shall be recorded, logs exported to the customer SIEM within 24 hours, and retained for a minimum of 7 years.

2) Customer-managed Keys & Escrow: Customer may elect to provide KEKs held in customer-managed KMS. If the customer elects redundant escrow, Redwood will deposit an encrypted recovery envelope with the mutually agreed escrow agent (TrustAudit). Release of the envelope requires (i) a signed release authorization from the customer admin named in the agreement and (ii) Redwood incident lead approval. The escrow agent acts only as custodian and cannot unilaterally release material.

Also added a short definition list (Breakglass Event, KEK, Escrow Agent) to avoid ambiguity. If MedVox accepts these two bullets we can incorporate them as an amendment and avoid redlining the rest of the DPA.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on keystore escrow / operator access for on-prem private deployment — consolidated position and next steps

Alex / MedVox team — thanks for the questions and the patience. Consolidated position below and next steps to keep procurement moving:

What we confirm today:
- Customer KEK supported; Redwood will not retain plaintext keys.
- Optional escrow available; escrow envelopes encrypted under the customer KEK and custodied by TrustAudit. Escrow release requires signed customer authorization + Redwood incident lead approval (as described by KarThik).
- Operator access restricted to documented Breakglass Events; two-party Redwood approval plus named customer admin sign-off required; sessions recorded and logs exportable to customer SIEM.
- Subprocessors: attached CSV lists current subprocessors; Redwood will contractually geofence replication/backups to US-only regions for MedVox if requested.
- Audit logs: KMS usage, operator sessions, and key activity events available; default retention 90 days with archives exportable up to 7 years.

Next steps / asks from MedVox:
1) Please confirm the primary customer admin names who can sign for escrow release and breakglass approvals (we will add them to the amendment).
2) Confirm whether DocuSign-per-incident is required or if a signed authorization + authenticated ticketing request is acceptable. KarThik noted DocuSign-only is operationally harder; we can accept it if specified in the contract with defined SLA windows.
3) If acceptable, we will circulate a one-page DPA amendment (attaching our proposed language) for MedVox review. Neha will shepherd it through legal.

I’ve attached the DPA amendment draft (DPA_redlines_MedVox_v1.docx) and the subprocessors CSV. If you’d like a quick call to walk the team through the breakglass flow, I’m available Thursday 10/18 09:00-11:00 PT.

If MedVox signs off on the amendment wording and provides admin names, procurement can proceed to DocuSign and we’ll schedule a short ops run-through.

Best,
